```{r}
# 1. Create a named list of all your model objects
all_models <- list(
  "spp_m" = spp_m,
  "k2m"   = k2m,   "k2ms"  = k2ms,
  "k3m"   = k3m,   "k3ms"  = k3ms,
  "k4m"   = k4m,   "k4ms"  = k4ms,
  "k5m"   = k5m,   "k5ms"  = km5s, 
  "k6m"   = k6m,   "k6ms"  = k6ms,
  "k7m"   = k7m,   "k7ms"  = k7ms,
  "k8m"   = k8m,   "k8ms"  = k8ms,
  "k9m"   = k9m,   "k9ms"  = k9ms,
  "k10m"  = k10m,  "k10ms" = k10ms,
  "k11m"  = k11m,  "k11ms" = k11ms,
  "k12m"  = k12m,  "k12ms" = k12ms,
  "k13m"  = k13m,  "k13ms" = k13ms,
  "k14m"  = k14m,  "k14ms" = k14ms,
  "k3msi" = k3msi, "k4msi" = k4msi
)

# 2. Extract AIC, BIC, and both R2 values together
master_model_table <- imap_dfr(all_models, function(model_obj, model_name) {
  
  # Grab information criteria
  perf <- model_performance(model_obj)
  
  # Grab variance partition metrics
  r2_vals <- r2(model_obj)
  
  data.frame(
    Model_Name      = model_name,
    AIC             = round(perf$AIC, 1),
    BIC             = round(perf$BIC, 1),
    Marginal_R2     = round(r2_vals$R2_marginal, 3),
    Conditional_R2  = round(r2_vals$R2_conditional, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

# 3. View the table sorted by AIC to look at the trade-offs cleanly
print(master_model_table %>% arrange(AIC))


#write.csv(master_model_table, here("Data", "master_model_table.csv"))

top_models <- list(
  "K3_plus_Spp"  = k3ms,
  "K4_plus_Spp"  = k4ms,
  "K_3_*_Spp"= k3msi,
  "Just_Spp" = spp_m
)

anova_table <- lapply(names(top_models), function(model_name) {
  m <- top_models[[model_name]]
  an <- anova(m)
  
  as.data.frame(an) %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    mutate(Model = model_name)
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  dplyr::select(Model, term, everything()) # Keeps it scannable

print(anova_table)

var_table <- imap_dfr(top_models, function(m, model_name) {
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))
  
  # Extract site variance safely
  site_var <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "site"] 
  if(length(site_var) == 0) site_var <- 0 # Fallback safety if variance is exactly 0
  
  # Extract residual variance
  resid_var <- attr(VarCorr(m), "sc")^2
  total <- site_var + resid_var
  
  tibble(
    Model             = model_name,
    Site_variance     = site_var,
    Residual_variance = resid_var,
    Site_prop         = site_var / total,
    Residual_prop     = resid_var / total
  )
})

print(var_table)

emmeans_table <- imap_dfr(top_models, function(m, model_name) {
  # Calculate post-hoc differences between your species lines
  em <- emmeans(m, ~ species)
  
  tidy(pairs(em)) %>%
    mutate(Model = model_name)
})

print(emmeans_table)
```

```{r}
#plot tom's "efficiency frontier"
library(ggrepel) # For non-overlapping labels

# 1. Prepare data (using Conditional_R2 as the primary metric)
# Change 'Conditional_R2' to 'Marginal_R2' if preferred
plot_data <- master_model_table %>%
  rename(R2_target = Conditional_R2)

# 2. Compute the Efficiency (Pareto) Frontier
# Sort by BIC ascending, then calculate cumulative max R2
frontier_data <- plot_data %>%
  arrange(BIC, desc(R2_target)) %>%
  mutate(cum_max_R2 = cummax(R2_target)) %>%
  filter(R2_target == cum_max_R2) %>%
  distinct(R2_target, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 3. Tag models in main table as Efficient vs. Suboptimal
plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(is_frontier = Model_Name %in% frontier_data$Model_Name)

# 4. Generate Efficiency Frontier Plot
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = BIC, y = R2_target)) +
  # Draw step line for efficiency frontier
  # geom_step(
  #   data = frontier_data,
  #   aes(x = BIC, y = R2_target),
  #   direction = "hv",
  #   color = "#1f77b4",
  #   linewidth = 1,
  #   linetype = "dashed"
  # ) +
  # Points for suboptimal models
  geom_point(
    data = filter(plot_data, !is_frontier),
    color = "gray60",
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  # Highlight points on the efficiency frontier
  geom_point(
    data = filter(plot_data, is_frontier),
    color = "#1f77b4",
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Model Labels (non-overlapping)
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = Model_Name, color = is_frontier),
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = ifelse(plot_data$is_frontier, "bold", "plain"),
    max.overlaps = 20,
    box.padding = 0.35
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#1f77b4", "FALSE" = "gray30")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Model Efficiency Frontier (BIC vs. Conditional R²)",
    #subtitle = "Dashed line marks Pareto-optimal models (higher R² for a given BIC penalty)",
    x = "BIC ",
    y = expression("Conditional " * R^2 * "")
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```
```{r}
#Single model:  ED50 ~ K_3 + (1 | site)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(resid(k3ms) ~ fitted(k3m), main = "Residuals vs Fitted (k3m)", xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residuals")
qqnorm(resid(k3m), main = "Normal Q-Q Plot (k3ms)")
qqline(resid(k3m), col = "red")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1)) 

#Test overall significance of single model
anova(k3m)  #(p=0.01815)

#  Compute EMMs & Significance Letters (Tukey adjusted) for single spp model
emm_k3 <- emmeans(k3m, ~ K_3)
performance(k3m)
anova(k3m)

#tukey adjustment
cld_k3 <- cld(emm_k3, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    K_3 = as.factor(K_3),
    .group = trimws(.group) # Cleans up any leading whitespace in letters
  )

#no adjustment
cld_k3_lsd <- cld(emm_k3, adjust = "none", Letters = letters) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    K_3 = as.factor(K_3),
    .group = trimws(.group)
  )


# Plot: ED50 by K_3 cluster with raw points + EMMs + Significance Letters
plot_k3 <- ggplot() +
  # Layer 1: Jittered raw data points (colored by species, shaped by site)
  geom_jitter(
    data = df_modeling,
    aes(x = as.factor(K_3), y = ED50, color = species, shape = as.factor(site)),
    width = 0.18,
    alpha = 0.65,
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  # Layer 2: Model summary (EMM black dots & 95% Confidence Intervals)
  geom_errorbar(
    data = cld_k3_lsd,
    aes(x = K_3, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.9,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = cld_k3_lsd,
    aes(x = K_3, y = emmean),
    size = 4,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Layer 3: Compact Letter Display (Significance letters placed above upper CI)
  geom_text(
    data = cld_k3_lsd,
    aes(x = K_3, y = upper.CL + 0.12, label = .group),
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 5.5,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Formatting & Styling
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
   # title = "Thermal Performance across Photophysiological Clusters",
   # subtitle = "Raw data colored by species; black points show unadjusted K_3 EMMs (± 95% CI)",
    x = "Photophysiological Cluster (K = 3)",
    y = expression(ED[50]~"("*degree*C*")"),
    color = "Species",
    shape = "Site"
  )+
  scale_shape_manual(values = custom_shapes) 

print(plot_k3)
```

```{r}
#BEST MODEL k3ms - yet confounding. 
# --- 1. Model Checks & ANOVA ---
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(resid(k3ms) ~ fitted(k3ms), main = "Residuals vs Fitted (k3ms)", xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residuals")
qqnorm(resid(k3ms), main = "Normal Q-Q Plot (k3ms)")
qqline(resid(k3ms), col = "red")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1)) 

#Test overall significance of single model
anova(k3ms)  #both are sig, p < 0.001

# --- 2. Extract EMMs &  Letter Display ---
k3ms_cluster_emm <- emmeans(k3ms, specs = ~ K_3) 

# Convert EMM to dataframe and compute CLD letters
cld_clusters <- cld(k3ms_cluster_emm, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    K_3 = as.factor(K_3),
    .group = trimws(.group)
  )

# --- 3. Generate Efficiency/Performance Plot with Raw Data ---
plot_k3ms <- ggplot() +
  # Layer A: Raw data jittered points (colored by species, shape by site)
  geom_jitter(
    data = df_modeling, 
    aes(x = as.factor(K_3), y = ED50, color = species, shape = site),
    width = 0.18, 
    alpha = 0.55, 
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  # Layer B: Model Estimated Marginal Means (Black points + Error bars)
  geom_errorbar(
    data = cld_clusters,
    aes(x = K_3, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    width = 0.12, 
    linewidth = 0.9, 
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = cld_clusters,
    aes(x = K_3, y = emmean),
    size = 4, 
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Layer C: Statistical significance letters (CLD)
  geom_text(
    data = cld_clusters,
    aes(x = K_3, y = upper.CL + 0.15, label = .group),
    fontface = "bold", 
    size = 5.5,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Styling & Labels
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
    #title = "Photophysiological Cluster Thermal Performance",
    #subtitle = "Controlling for species identity; species:K_3 interaction non-significant (p = 0.36)",
    x = "Photophysiological Cluster (K = 3)",
    y = expression(Estimated~Marginal~Mean~ED50~"("*degree*C*")"),
    color = "Species",
    shape = "Site"
  )+
  scale_shape_manual(values = custom_shapes) 

print(plot_k3ms)
```

```{r}
# Print this out to verify the column names before plotting!

cld_spp_plot <- cld_spp %>%

  )

df_raw_clean <- df_modeling %>%
  mutate(
    species = toupper(species),
    K_3 = factor(paste("Cluster", K_3))
  )

# 2. Clean the EMMeans CLD data frame identically
cld_spp_plot <- cld_spp %>%
  mutate(
    species = toupper(species),
    K_3 = factor(paste("Cluster", K_3)),
    .group = trimws(as.character(.group))
  )

# 3. Dynamic layout math for text placement
y_range <- max(cld_spp_plot$upper.CL, na.rm = TRUE) - min(cld_spp_plot$lower.CL, na.rm = TRUE)
text_offset <- y_range * 0.06

# 4. Generate the combined plot
plot_jittered <- ggplot() +
  # STEP A: Plot the raw data points in the background (jittered horizontally)
  geom_jitter(
    data = df_raw_clean, 
    aes(x = species, y = ED50, color = species),
    alpha = 0.35,       # Makes raw data slightly transparent
    width = 0.2,        # Spread of the jittering
    height = 0          # Do not jitter vertically (keeps true ED50 values)
  ) +
  # STEP B: Layer the EMMeans model results explicitly on top using a separate dataset
  geom_errorbar(
    data = cld_spp_plot,
    aes(x = species, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    color = "black", width = 0.15, linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = cld_spp_plot,
    aes(x = species, y = emmean, fill = species),
    color = "black", shape = 21, size = 4.5, stroke = 1.5
  ) +
  # STEP C: Add the post-hoc significance letter labels
  geom_text(
    data = cld_spp_plot,
    aes(x = species, y = upper.CL + text_offset, label = .group), 
    color = "black", fontface = "bold", size = 5
  ) +
  # Split into identical grid panels by cluster
  facet_wrap(~ K_3) + 
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank() # Cleans up vertical grid lines
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Species Identity",
    y = expression(ED[50]~"("*degree*C*")")
  )

  # Faceting by Cluster showcases the additive shift clearly
  facet_wrap(~ paste("Cluster", K_3), nrow = 1) +
  
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey93", color = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Additive Model Fit Across Subgroups",
    subtitle = "Letters compare species WITHIN each specific cluster panel",
    x = "Species Identity",
    y = expression(Estimated~Marginal~Mean~ED[50]~"("*degree*C*")")
  )

print(plot_joint_emm)
```

```{r}
# 3. Dynamic layout math for text placement

    data = cld_spp_plot,
```

```{r}
# Loop through and compute AIC using lmer()
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(lme4)
library(performance)

model_comp <- map_df(k_cols, function(k_name) {
  
  # Fit the model (REML = FALSE is mandatory for comparing fixed structures via AIC)
  form <- as.formula(paste("ED50 ~ species +", k_name, "+ (1 | site)"))
  model <- lmer(form, data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)
  
  # Grab AIC and BIC
  perf <- model_performance(model)
  
  data.frame(
    Model          = k_name,
    AIC            = perf$AIC,
    BIC            = perf$BIC,           # Punishes overfitting harder than AIC
    R2_Marginal    = perf$R2_marginal,    # Variance explained by Species + K-Cluster
    R2_Conditional = perf$R2_conditional  # Total variance explained including Site
  )
})

# Arrange by best AIC to see the trade-offs
print(model_comp %>% arrange(AIC))

# 1. Fit the final, optimal model structure
final_model <- lmer(ED50 ~ species + K_5 + (1 | site), 
                    data = df_modeling, 
                    REML = TRUE)

# 2. Look at the coefficients to see WHICH clusters are more tolerant
summary(final_model)

# 3. Check exactly how much heat tolerance separates the groups (in degrees C)
tidy(k2ms, effects = "fixed")

table(df_modeling$species, df_modeling$K_5)

emm_K4 <- emmeans(final_model, ~ K_5)
pairs(emm_K4, adjust = "tukey")

emm_spp <- emmeans(final_model, ~ species)
pairs(emm_spp, adjust = "tukey")

# emm_joint <- emmeans(final_model, ~ species | K_3)
# pairs(emm_joint, adjust = "tukey") #cant do interaction. few overlap


#plot

# 1. Convert EMMs to a readable dataframe
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emmeans(final_model, ~ K_3))

# 2. Build the plot
ggplot() +
  # Draw the raw data points in the background (jittered to prevent overlapping)
  geom_jitter(data = df_modeling, 
              aes(x = K_3, y = ED50, color = species), 
              alpha = 0.4, width = 0.2, height = 0) +
  
  # Draw the model's EMMs as large point estimates
  geom_point(data = emm_df, 
             aes(x = K_3, y = emmean, group = species), 
             color = "black", size = 4, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  
  # Add Confidence Interval error bars from the model
  geom_errorbar(data = emm_df, 
                aes(x = K_3, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL, group = species), 
                color = "black", width = 0.1, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  
  # Clean up formatting
  #facet_wrap(~ species) + 
  labs(title = "Model EMMs (with 95% CI) vs. Raw ED50 Data",
       x = "Cluster (K_3)",
       y = "ED50 (°C)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
  geom_errorbar(data = emm2,
                aes(K_3,
                    ymin = lower.CL,
                    ymax = upper.CL),
                width = 0.12,
                linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Photophysiological Cluster",
       y = expression(ED[50]~degree*C)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)
```

```{r}
#plot predictions

# 1. Extract predictions (fitted values) from your final model
df_modeling$Predicted_ED50 <- predict(final_model)

# 2. Plot Raw vs. Predicted
plot_pred_vs_raw <- ggplot(df_modeling, aes(x = Predicted_ED50, y = ED50)) +
  # Add a 1:1 line. If predictions were perfect, dots would sit exactly on this line
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "darkred", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # Scatter dots colored by Species and shaped by Cluster Group
  geom_point(aes(color = toupper(species), shape = as.factor(K_3)), size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Add a trend line of your actual fit to see deviation from the 1:1 line
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "darkblue", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Model Validation: Predicted vs. Observed Heat Tolerance",
    subtitle = "Dashed Line = Perfect 1:1 Prediction | Solid Line = Actual Model Fit",
    x = expression("Predicted " * ED[50] * " (°C)"),
    y = expression("Observed Raw " * ED[50] * " (°C)"),
    color = "Species",
    shape = "K_3 Cluster"
  )

# Display the plot
print(plot_pred_vs_raw)

# Save to your plots directory
ggsave(here("Plots", "ED50_Predicted_vs_Raw.png"), plot = plot_pred_vs_raw, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
r2_vals <- model_performance(model)

test_residuals <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = model)
plot(test_residuals)

k3_m <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_3 + species + (1 | site), data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)
k10_m <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_10 + species + (1 | site), data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)
k8_m  <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_8 + species + (1 | site),  data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)

# 2. Run the comparative ANOVA (Likelihood Ratio Test)
anova(k3_m, k10_m, k8_m)
#10 is lowest aic when 
summary(k11_m)
summary(k12_m)
summary(k4_m)

r2(k11_m) #conditional () = 0.514, marginal (sites) = 0.242. So, fixed effect explains 17% of variance, site explains 22.5% (39.4-16.9)
r2(k12_m) #conditional () = 0.395, marginal () = 0.170
r2(k4_m) #conditional () = 0.379, marginal () = 0.087
# 1. Calculate the estimated marginal means for each cluster group
k11_means <- emmeans(k11_m, specs = ~ K_11)


# 2. Run the pairwise post-hoc comparisons with Tukey adjustment
k11_posthoc <- pairs(k11_means, adjust = "tukey")

# 3. View the results
# (Optional: filter for only statistically significant differences)
k11_posthoc_df <- as.data.frame(k11_posthoc)

significant_differences <- k11_posthoc_df %>% 
  filter(p.value < 0.05)

print(significant_differences)
pairs(emmeans(k11_m, ~ K_11))
plot(k11_means, comparisons = TRUE)

# Plot residuals against fitted values
plot(k11_m, type = c("p", "smooth"), 
     xlab = "Fitted Values (Predicted ED50)", 
     ylab = "Residuals")

res <- residuals(k11_m)

# Create Q-Q plot
qqnorm(res, main = "Normal Q-Q Plot of Residuals")

custom_order <- c("1", "2", "3", "4",  "9", "7","10", "11", "5", "6",  "8") #make plot then change these if needed

#change order
df_modeling$K_11 <- factor(df_modeling$K_11, levels = custom_order)

# 2. Re-run emmeans (it will automatically adopt the new factor order)
k11_predicted <- as.data.frame(emmeans(k11_m, ~ K_11))


# 2. Plot raw data as points, and model predictions as larger points with error bars
ggplot() +
  # Raw data points (colored by site to see the random effect)
  geom_jitter(data = df_modeling, aes(x = K_11, y = ED50, color = species, shape = site), alpha = 0.5, width = 0.2, size = 3) +
  # Model predictions (Emmeans)
  geom_point(data = k11_predicted, aes(x = K_11, y = emmean), size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(data = k11_predicted, aes(x = K_11, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), 
                color = "black", width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Model Fit: Raw ED50 Data vs. Model Predictions",
       x = "K_11 Category",
       y = "ED50")
```

```{r}
# 1. Correct the CLD call to use the EMM object
cld_clusters <- cld(k4ms_cluster_emm, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters) %>%
  mutate(.group = trimws(.group))

# 2. Generate Plot
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. Generate the CLD letters for the clusters ---
cld_clusters <- cld(k4ms_cluster_emm, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters) %>%
  mutate(.group = trimws(.group))

# --- 2. Build the Layered Plot ---
plot_cluster_with_raw <- ggplot() +
  
  # LAYER 1: Raw data points in the background, jittered and colored by species
  geom_jitter(data = df_modeling %>% filter(!is.na(K_3)), 
              aes(x = as.factor(K_4), y = ED50, color = species),
              width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4, size = 2.5) +
  
  # LAYER 2: Model-estimated marginal means (large open diamond)
  geom_point(data = cld_clusters, 
             aes(x = as.factor(K_4), y = emmean), 
             size = 4.5, shape = 18, color = "black") +
  
  # LAYER 3: 95% Confidence Intervals calculated from the model
  geom_errorbar(data = cld_clusters, 
                aes(x = as.factor(K_4), ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), 
                width = 0.12, linewidth = 1.1, color = "black") +
  
  # LAYER 4: Post-hoc significance letters mapped cleanly above the error bars
  geom_text(data = cld_clusters, 
            aes(x = as.factor(K_4), y = upper.CL + 0.15, label = .group), 
            fontface = "bold", size = 5, color = "black") +
  
  # Formatting & Aesthetics
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Physiological Cluster Thermal Performance",
    subtitle = "Diamonds show model means (95% CI) over raw biological points",
    x = "Photophysiological Cluster Assignment (K=3)",
    y = expression(ED[50]~"("*degree*C*")"),
    color = "Coral Species"
  )

# Display the plot
print(plot_cluster_with_raw)

# Save the plot
ggsave(here("Plots", "EMM_Clusters_K3_with_RawData.png"), 
       plot = plot_cluster_with_raw, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```
